Based on the investigation of the support workspace:

1. **Sender Transmission & Envelope Verification**:
   - In session `S1827` at `07:54:42`, Tidewell's gateway (`O0013TIDEWELL3884`) connected to the Brannock EDI Exchange clearing centre (`O0013BRANNOCK3666`) and transmitted `INV45911.edi` (401 octets) with `SFIDDSN` = `TIDEWELL.INVOIC`, `SFIDDATE` = `20261030`, `SFIDTIME` = `0753270001`, `SFIDDEST` = `O0013CORRANDALE5887`, and `SFIDORIG` = `O0013TIDEWELL3884`.
   - All OFTP2 session and virtual file parameters match the partner agreement with Corrandale Truck Plant. The clearing centre positively acknowledged the end of file (`EFPA` `4N`).
   - The wire copy (`/outbound-wire/INV45911.edi`) is a valid EDIFACT interchange matching every requirement of the partner agreement (`UNOA:3`, sender `TIDEWELL71:ZZ`, recipient `CORRANDALE37:ZZ`, `INVOIC:D:96A:UN`, matching `UNB`/`UNZ` control reference `390269`, segment count `19` in `UNT`, and message count `1` in `UNZ`).

2. **Ambiguity Between Clearing Centre and Final Recipient**:
   - No EERP, NERP, or `CONTRL` message has been received by Tidewell, and Corrandale's accounts payable team states they have not seen the invoice.
   - Because the file passes through the Brannock EDI Exchange clearing centre (`O0013BRANNOCK3666`), and we only have Tidewell's gateway trace, it is not yet determinable whether the clearing centre failed to forward the file to Corrandale (`intermediary_fault`), or whether the clearing centre delivered it to Corrandale and Corrandale failed to return the EERP / process it on their side.
   - Checking the clearing centre's trace (`request_clearing_centre_trace`) is required to determine whether the file was forwarded to and accepted by Corrandale.

# Ticket U3 (agentic)

You work on the EDI support desk that serves the sender of the file described
below. A customer has raised the ticket that follows. Everything you need to
diagnose it is in the support workspace, which you can explore only with the
tools list_dir, read_file and search (start with /README.txt). The workspace
also holds unrelated material. All companies, identifiers and documents are
synthetic. You may use at most 25 tool calls; then give your final answer.

## The ticket

```text
From: Robin Novak, EDI desk, Tidewell Seating Components
Subject: no EERP for invoice INV45911

The Brannock EDI Exchange clearing centre accepted our invoice INV45911 for Corrandale Truck Plant at 07:53 this morning. More than three hours later there is still no EERP, although the agreement says two hours, and Corrandale Truck Plant say they have not seen the invoice. Our files through the same clearing centre to Calderbank Wiring were all acknowledged this morning, so the clearing centre works. Corrandale Truck Plant must have lost it. Please find the root cause and tell us who has to fix it.
```

## What to return

Diagnose the single root cause of this ticket. Reply in any form you like,
but end your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block holding an object
with these six keys. Only the last ```json block in your reply is graded.
Give one value per key: a key that holds several options, or a list of
alternatives, scores zero for that key.

cause: exactly one of
  authentication_failure: The OFTP2 session could not be established because a password, identification code or secure authentication check failed.
  certificate_problem: A TLS or file-security certificate is expired, untrusted or not the one in the agreement.
  character_set_violation: The interchange contains characters outside the agreed syntax identifier's character repertoire.
  compression_not_agreed: A file was sent compressed (or uncompressed) contrary to what the receiver accepts.
  duplicate_interchange: An interchange was rejected because its interchange control reference was already received from this sender.
  duplicate_virtual_file: A virtual file was refused because a virtual file with the same identification was already delivered.
  end_to_end_response_not_returned: The file was delivered but the final recipient never returned the end-to-end response.
  envelope_element_format_invalid: A UNB or UNZ data element has a value whose format or length the syntax version declared in UNB S001 does not allow.
  file_too_large: The file exceeds a size limit of the receiver.
  interchange_control_count_mismatch: The interchange control count in UNZ does not match the number of messages in the interchange.
  interchange_control_reference_mismatch: The interchange control reference in UNB and in UNZ are not identical.
  intermediary_fault: A clearing centre or other intermediate location lost, altered or misrouted the file.
  invalid_destination: The OFTP2 destination of the virtual file is not known to the receiver.
  no_sender_side_fault: Nothing the sender transmitted is wrong; the fault lies with the receiver.
  not_yet_determinable: The documents fit more than one root cause equally well, so the root cause cannot be named until a further check is made.
  recipient_identification_mismatch: The interchange recipient identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  restart_position_invalid: A restarted transfer used a restart position that is wrong, or resumed from a position other than the one the receiver confirmed.
  sender_identification_mismatch: The interchange sender identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  session_parameters_not_negotiated: The sender used an OFTP2 session parameter (credit, buffer size or similar) outside what was negotiated.
  syntax_identifier_not_agreed: UNB S001 declares a syntax identifier or syntax version other than the agreed one.
  test_indicator_mismatch: The interchange is flagged as test (or production) contrary to the agreement.

layer: exactly one of
  transport: The OFTP2 session or file transfer, including any intermediate location.
  envelope: The EDIFACT interchange envelope (UNB to UNZ), wherever the receiver checks it (gateway or translator).
  none: There is no fault on the sender side.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

owner: exactly one of (who must act to fix the root cause)
  sender: The party that sent the file and raised the ticket must fix it.
  receiver: The trading partner the file is addressed to must fix it.
  intermediary: A clearing centre or other intermediate location between the parties must fix it.
  agreement: The partner agreement itself is wrong or inconsistent and must be amended before either side can fix the fault.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

location: a JSON array of strings.
List the OFTP2 fields or EDIFACT data elements whose values must be changed to
fix the root cause, and no others. If the fault is a conflict between two values
that must agree, list both. Write each one as:
  OFTP2 field:                 COMMAND.FIELD, e.g. "SSID.SSIDCODE"
  EDIFACT simple data element: SEGMENT.ELEMENT, e.g. "UNH.0062"
  EDIFACT component element:   SEGMENT.COMPOSITE.COMPONENT, e.g. "UNB.S003.0010"
  No fault on the sender side: "NONE" on its own.
  Root cause not yet determinable: "UNDETERMINED" on its own.

next_check: exactly one of (the single check that would decide the root cause if the documents do not; "none" if they do)
  none: The documents already determine the root cause.
  request_receiver_gateway_log: Ask the receiver for its OFTP2 gateway log covering the file in question.
  request_receiver_translator_log: Ask the receiver for its translator's validation log for the interchange.
  request_transmitted_copy: Obtain the file exactly as the sender's gateway transmitted it, not the archived copy.
  request_other_gateway_node_trace: Obtain the trace from the sender's other gateway node or nodes.
  request_agreement_in_force: Obtain the signed version of the partner agreement currently in force.
  request_clearing_centre_trace: Ask the clearing centre for its trace of the file.
  check_sender_clock: Check the sender gateway's system clock.
  check_certificates: Check the TLS and file-security certificates on both sides.
  resend_unchanged: Send the same file again unchanged.
  resend_with_new_identity: Send the file again as a new virtual file.

value: a JSON string holding the SFIDTIME of the virtual file that has no EERP.

Example of the format only (not a hint):
```json
{"cause": "file_too_large", "layer": "transport", "owner": "receiver", "location": ["SFID.SFIDFSIZ"], "next_check": "none", "value": "12345"}
```

1: RFC 5024 (ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 2), section 4.3.6. Verbatim extract.
2: 
3: 4.3.6.  End to End Response (EERP)
4: 
5:    The End to End Response (EERP) command notifies the originator of a
6:    Virtual File that the Virtual File has been successfully delivered to
7:    its final destination.  This allows the originator to perform house
8:    keeping tasks such as deleting copies of the delivered data.
9: 
10:    If the originator of the Virtual File requested a signed EERP in the
11:    SFID, the EERP must be signed.  Signing allows the originator of the
12:    file to prove that the EERP was generated by the final destination.
13:    If the final destination is unable to sign the EERP, it may send back
14:    an unsigned EERP.  It is an implementation issue to allow the
15:    acceptance of an unsigned EERP if a signed EERP is requested.
16: 
17:    A Response Command must be sent from the location performing the
18:    final processing or distribution of the data to the originator.  The
19:    Response is mandatory and may be sent in the same or in any
20:    subsequent session.
21: 
22:    When an intermediate location broadcasts or distributes a Virtual
23:    File, it must receive a Response command from all the locations to
24:    which it forwarded the data before sending its own Response.  This
25:    ensures that the Response received by the Virtual File's originator
26:    accounts for all the destination locations.  An intermediate location
27:    therefore needs to track the status of files it processes over time.
28: 
29:    The requesting of a signed EERP is incompatible with the use of
30:    broadcast facilities because an EERP can be signed by only one
31:    destination.  If this scenario occurs, the intermediate broadcast
32:    location may continue and ignore the request for a signed EERP or
33:    send back a NERP.
34: 
35:    Example: Point to Point
36: 
37:       Location A sends file Ba to location B, which will send an EERP to
38:       location A after it successfully receives the file.
39: 
40:          o----------o                          o-----------o
41:          | Loc. A   |----------- S1 ---------->| Loc. B    |
42:          |          |                          |           |
43:          | [Ba]     |<---------- R2 -----------| [Ba]      |
44:          +----------o                          o-----------o
45: 
46:                      Key:   S - File Transfer
47:                             R - Response EERP
48:                          [Ba] - File for B from A
49: 
50:    Example: Data distribution
51: 
52:       Location A sends a Virtual File containing data for distribution
53:       to locations B and C via clearing centres E1 and E2.  Clearing
54:       centre E1 must wait for a response from E2 (for file Ba) and
55:       location C before it sends its response, R8, to location A.
56:       Clearing centre E2 can only send response R7 to E1 when location B
57:       acknowledges file Ba with response R6.
58: 
59:    o---------o        o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
60:    | Loc. A  |-- S1 ->| Loc. E1 |-- S2 ->| Loc. E2 |-- S5 ->| Loc. B  |
61:    |         |        |         |        |         |        |         |
62:    | [Ba,Ca] |<- R8 --| [Ba,Ca] |<- R7 --| [Ba]    |<- R6 --| [Ba]    |
63:    o---------o        o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
64:                          A   |
65:                          |   |           o---------o
66:                          |   +----- S3 ->| Loc. C  |
67:                          |               |         |
68:                          +--------- R4 --| [Ca]    |
69:                                          o---------o
70: 
71:    Example: Data collection
72: 
73:       Locations A and B send files Ca and Cb to clearing centre E1,
74:       which forwards both files to location C in a single Virtual File.
75:       When it receives response R4 from C, clearing centre E1 sends
76:       response R5 to location A and R6 to location B.
77: 
78:          o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
79:          | Loc. A  |-- S1 ->| Loc. E1 |-- S3 ->| Loc. C  |
80:          |         |        |         |        |         |
81:          | [Ca]    |<- R5 --| [Ca,Cb] |<- R4 --| [Ca,Cb] |
82:          o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
83:                                A   |
84:          o---------o           |   |
85:          | Loc. B  |-- S2 -----+   |
86:          |         |               |
87:          | [Cb]    |<- R6 ---------+
88:          o---------o
